source_text:
Ὡς μακάρια καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ δῶρα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀγαπητοί.
ζωὴ ἐν ἀθανασίᾳ, λαμπρότης ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ἀλήθεια ἐν παρρησίᾳ, πίστις ἐν πεποιθήσει, ἐγκράτεια ἐν ἁγιασμῷ: καὶ ταῦτα ὑπέπιπτεν πάντα ὑπὸ τὴν διάνοιαν ἡμῶν.
τίνα οὖν ἄρα ἐστὶν τὰ ἑτοιμαζόμενα τοῖς ὑπομένουσιν; ὁ δημιουργὸς καὶ πατὴρ τῶν αἰώνων ὁ πανάγιος αὐτὸς γινώσκει τὴν ποσότητα καὶ τὴν καλλονὴν αὐτῶν.
ἡμεῖς οὖν ἀγωνισώμεθα εὑρεθῆναι ἐν τῷ ἀριθμῷ τῶν ὑπομενόντων, ὅπως μεταλάβωμεν τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων δωρεῶν.
πῶς δὲ ἔσται τοῦτο, ἀγαπητοί; ἐὰν ἐστηριγμενη ᾖ ἡ διάνοια ἡμῶν πιστῶς πρὸς τὸν θεόν, ἐὰν ἐκζητῶμεν τὰ εὐάρεστα καὶ εὐπρόσδεκτα αὐτῷ, ἐὰν ἐπιτελέσωμεν τὰ ἀνήκοντα τῇ ἀμώμῳ βουλήσει αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθήσωμεν τῇ ὁδῷ τῆς ἀληθείας, ἀπορρίψαντες ἀφ̓ ἑαυτῶν πᾶσαν ἀδικίαν καὶ πονηρίαν, πλεονεξίαν, ἔρεις, κακοηθείας τε καὶ δόλους, ψιθυρισμούς τε καὶ καταλαλιάς, θεοστυγίαν, ὑπερηφανίαν τε καὶ ἀλαζονείαν, κενοδοξίαν τε καὶ ἀφιλοξενίαν.
ταῦτα γὰρ οἱ πράσσοντες στυγητοὶ τῷ θεῷ ὑπάρχουσιν: οὐ μόνον δὲ οἱ πράσσοντες αὐτά, ἀλλά καὶ οἱ συνευδοκοῦντες αὐτοῖς.
λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός: Ἱνατί σὺ διηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου, καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τὴν διαθήκην μου ἐπὶ στόματός σου;
σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν καὶ ἐξέβαλες τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω. εἰ ἐθεώρεις κλέπτην. συνέτρεχες αὐτῷ, καὶ μετὰ μοιχῶν τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις. τὸ στόμα σου ἐπλεόνασεν κακίαν, καὶ ή γλῶσσα σου περιέπλεκεν δολιότητα. καθήμενος κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου κατελάλεις, καὶ κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς μητρός σου ἐτίθεις σκάνδαλον.
ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα: ὑπέλαβες, ἄνομε, ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος.
ἐλέγξω σε καὶ παραστήσω σε κατὰ προσωπόν σου.
σύνετε δὴ ταῦτα, οἱ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι τοῦ θεοῦ. μήποτε ἁρπάσῃ ὡς λέων, καὶ μὴ ᾖ ὁ ῥυόμενος.
θυσία αἰνέσεως δοξάσει με, καὶ ἐκεῖ ὁδός, ᾗ δείξω αὐτῷ τὸ σωτήριον τοῦ θεοῦ.
thought_title: The Gifts of God and the Way to Receive Them
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, has just quoted Scripture about the glory of God's promises and now describes the gifts God has prepared for those who endure.
pass_a_gloss: How blessed and wonderful [are] the gifts of God, beloved. Life in immortality, brightness in righteousness, truth in boldness, faith in confidence, self-control in holiness: and these things all fell under our understanding. What then indeed are the things being prepared for those who endure? The creator and father of the ages, the all-holy one, himself knows their quantity and their beauty. We therefore let us strive to be found in the number of those who endure, so that we may share in the promised gifts. How then will this be, beloved? If our understanding is fixed faithfully toward God, if we seek the things pleasing and acceptable to him, if we accomplish the things belonging to his blameless will, and follow the way of truth, having thrown away from ourselves all unrighteousness and wickedness, greed, strife, malice and deceit, whisperings and slanders, hatred of God, pride and arrogance, vainglory and inhospitality. For those who practice these things are hateful to God; not only those who practice them, but also those who approve of them. For the Scripture says: To the sinner God said: Why do you recount my ordinances, and take up my covenant upon your mouth? But you hated discipline and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and with adulterers you placed your portion. Your mouth abounded in evil, and your tongue wove deceit. Sitting against your brother you slandered, and against the son of your mother you placed a stumbling block. These things you did, and I was silent; you supposed, lawless one, that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set you before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest he seize like a lion, and there be no one to rescue. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is a way by which I will show him the salvation of God.

choices.why: The noun denotes freedom of speech and confident openness before God, not mere frankness; 'boldness' captures the confident access implied in the context of divine gifts.

choices.term: ὑπέπιπτεν πάντα ὑπὸ τὴν διάνοιαν ἡμῶν
choices.why: The imperfect verb indicates these gifts were already accessible to human comprehension; 'fell under' preserves the spatial metaphor of the Greek.
The aorist subjunctive hortatory expresses an earnest call to effort; 'strive' conveys the athletic and moral struggle implied by the verb.
The compound noun means active hatred toward God, not merely being hateful to God; the rendering keeps the direction of the hatred clear.
The participle denotes consenting approval of the deeds, not mere passive tolerance; 'approve of' captures the active endorsement.
The phrase is a Hebraism meaning to confront someone with their own deeds; the literal rendering preserves the vivid courtroom image of the source.

pass_b_english: How blessed and wonderful, beloved, are the gifts of God! Life in immortality, splendor in righteousness, truth with boldness, faith with confidence, self-control with holiness: all these already lie within our understanding. What, then, is being prepared for those who endure? The all-holy Creator and Father of the ages himself knows how great and how beautiful those things are. So let us strive to be found among those who endure, that we may share in the gifts he has promised.

And how shall this be, beloved? It will be if our mind is set faithfully on God; if we seek what pleases him and what he accepts; if we carry out what fits his blameless will and follow the way of truth, casting away from us all wrongdoing and wickedness, greed, quarrels, malice and deceit, gossip and slander, hatred of God, pride and boasting, empty glory and want of hospitality. For those who do these things are hateful to God, and not only those who do them, but those who approve of them as well.

For the Scripture says: “But to the sinner God said: ‘What right have you to recite my statutes, or to take my covenant on your lips? You hated instruction and threw my words behind you. When you saw a thief, you ran along with him, and you threw in your lot with adulterers. Your mouth overflowed with evil, and your tongue wove deceit. You sat and slandered your brother, and laid a stumbling block before your own mother's son. You did these things, and I kept silent; you thought, lawless one, that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set you before your own face. Consider this, you who forget God, lest he seize you like a lion, with no one to rescue you. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God’” (Psalm 50:16-23).
